operation.description:
Returns the workspace brand kit. Until it is saved, it holds the defaults: an empty `theme`, no `name`, logo, links, header or footer, and `updatedAt` null. Every email's `theme` holds only the fields it overrides; the rest come from here. A `header` block without an image shows the brand kit's logo, and a `social` block without links shows its social links. A change restyles templates and draft campaigns and journeys at once. Scheduling or sending a campaign, activating a journey and publishing a template freeze the brand kit that email goes out with, so nothing already approved changes. The default header and footer are what gallery and Kiro designs open and close with; emails that place them follow the shared blocks' own changes.

Requires API-key scope: `templates:read`.

Lists everything activating now would refuse, all at once and without activating: unfinished send steps, a list, segment, form, topic or webhook a step, the trigger or an exit names that is gone or off, a conversion goal exit without a goal, and for each finished send step an unverified sender or a sending domain without the DMARC record marketing email needs, the workspace's missing postal address or a push app not ready. Each issue gives the field to fix, the error code `activateJourney` would answer with for it and, on a step, the step's id. Empty `issues` means these checks pass; activation can still refuse for the plan's active journey limit or, for a journey an agent authored or edited, a person's confirmation. An ended journey has one issue on `status`; a workspace whose sending is stopped (suspended, or its deletion pending) has one on `workspace`.

Requires API-key scope: `journeys:read`.

allDirectChanges.before:
Splits a campaign's email results into rows by the recipient's email domain (`gmail.com`), the device they first opened or clicked on (`desktop`, `mobile`, `tablet`), or the contact's country (`NG`), counted the same way as the campaign's metrics. Use it to find where a problem sits: bounces concentrated on one domain point at that mailbox provider, not at the whole list.

Rows are ordered by messages sent, largest first. The 50 largest are listed, and everything past them is summed in `other` (null when there are none). A row's `key` is `null` when the value is unknown: a device is known only once a person opens with images on or clicks (Apple Mail Privacy Protection's automatic opens and Gmail's image proxy name no device, and other image proxies may read as desktop); a country only when the contact has one; a domain only while the message still names someone (not after the contact is deleted).

Push results are not included: a push campaign's per-device outcomes are in its metrics, under `push.devices`.

Requires API-key scope: `campaigns:read`.

allDirectChanges.before:
Lists what each device reported for one push message: any message whose `channel` is `push`, from a campaign, a journey or a transactional send. A push reaches every ready installation of the contact, so a message has one delivery per device. `accepted`: Apple, Google or the browser's push service took it, which is not proof the device showed it. `invalid`: the device is gone and its installation was retired. `rejected`: refused, often the app's key or a payload the provider would not take. `retryable`: will be tried again. `unknown`: the provider may have taken it, so it is not resent. `skipped`: not attempted, as when the app's key was refused for another device of the same app. `pending` and `started` are still in flight. A message that is not a push returns 404.

Requires API-key scope: `messages:read`.

allDirectChanges.before:
Sends a one-off message to one recipient — a receipt, a password reset, a confirmation — bypassing campaigns. It ignores marketing preferences (it is the critical tier) but respects suppression. Agent keys are refused with 403.

**Channels.** Give `email`, `push`, or both. With both, `deliver: all` (the default) sends each one the contact can receive, and `deliver: first` sends push when the contact has a reachable device and email otherwise. A channel the contact cannot receive is passed over; only when none is left does the send fail, with that channel's reason. The response lists one message per channel sent.

**Data.** `data` holds the values the content reads as `{{ data.<key> }}`, once for every channel: a stored template, inline email, and the push `title` and `body`. Inline content (email or push) whose `{{ data.<key> }}` tag has no value in `data`, and no default, is refused with 400 rather than sent blank.

**Email.** Inline (`subject`, `from`, `html`, optional `text`, `previewText`, `replyTo`), or a stored template named by `template` (its alias, such as `password-reset`, or its id). The template's published version is rendered when the request is accepted and supplies the envelope; each envelope field given overrides it. The result needs a `subject` and a `from` (409 `TEMPLATE_ENVELOPE_INCOMPLETE`), and the `from` domain must be verified. A template never published is 409 `TEMPLATE_NOT_PUBLISHED`. Email is tracked only when `tracking` asks, and never for a contact in the EEA or the UK; `threading` continues a conversation. `attachments`, `threading` and `tracking` sit inside `email`.

**Push.** `push` takes the notification fields (`title`, `body`, `actionUrl`, …) beside `pushProjectId`, which is needed only when the workspace has several push projects.

**Recipient.** `to` names one `contactId`, `externalId` or `email`, and nothing else: set a contact's name or attributes with `POST /v1/contacts/identify` first. An `email` that matches no contact creates one for transactional mail only.

**Retries.** Send an `Idempotency-Key` header to make a retry safe. A retry with the same key and request returns the first result, with `Idempotency-Replay: true`, and sends nothing again; the same key with a different request is 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`. Without a key, every request sends: a retry after a timeout can send the message twice. A replay answers from the messages as they are now, so its `status` can differ from the first answer, and an `externalId` or `email` recipient the first request created or updated stays so even when the send itself was refused. Set `correlationId` to your own reference: it is echoed on each message's webhooks and its read, and `GET /v1/messages?correlationId=` finds them. `sendAt` times the send, email and push alike.

Requires API-key scope: `transactional:send`.
allDirectChanges.after:
Sends a one-off message to one recipient — a receipt, a password reset, a confirmation — bypassing campaigns. It ignores marketing preferences (it is the critical tier) but respects suppression. Agent keys are refused with 403.

**Channels.** Give `email`, `push`, or both. With both, `deliver: "all"` (the default) sends each one the contact can receive. `deliver: { "first": ["email", "push"] }` tries them in that order: the first the contact can receive goes, and each later one waits as a fallback (`fallbackFor`), sent only when the one before it fails, is skipped or bounces (an email gets 15 minutes to bounce), else skipped with reason `fallback_not_needed`. A fallback is charged only when it goes; with no room left in the plan by then it is skipped with reason `plan_limit_reached`. A channel the contact cannot receive, or the plan has no room for, is passed over and listed in `skippedChannels` with its error code; only when none is left does the send fail, with that channel's error. So with `all` too, a 202 can leave a channel unsent: check `skippedChannels`. The response lists one message per channel stored.

**Data.** `data` holds the values the content reads as `{{ data.<key> }}`, once for every channel: a stored template, inline email, and the push `title` and `body`. Inline content (email or push) whose `{{ data.<key> }}` tag has no value in `data`, and no default, is refused with 400 rather than sent blank.

**Push.** `push` takes the notification fields (`title`, `body`, `actionUrl`, …) beside `pushProjectId`, which is needed only when the workspace has several push projects. Unlike email, push needs the contact's push consent (`consent.push`) besides a device that allows notifications.

**Recipient.** `to` names one `contactId`, `externalId` or `email`, and nothing else: set a contact's name or attributes with `POST /v1/contacts/identify` first. An `email` that matches no contact creates one for transactional mail only.

updatedAt.description: Null until the brand kit is saved.

band.description: `insufficient_data` until the sample and feedback coverage minimums are met; then the highest line the bounce or complaint ratio reaches.

bounceRatio.description: Recorded bounces per sent email, the figure the band compares with `limits`; `null` while `sampleSize` is 0.

complaintRatio.description: Recorded complaints per sent email, the figure the band compares with `limits`; `null` while `sampleSize` is 0.

sampleSize.description: Sent emails the band is judged on: real sends only, with test sends that act an outcome out (`delivered@`, `bounce@`, `complaint@example.com`) left out.

minimumSampleSize.description: The fewest emails (`sampleSize`) the band is judged on, currently 100: below it the band is `insufficient_data`.

feedbackCoverage.description: Share of the sample whose outcome (delivered, bounced or complained) is known; `null` before any email is sent.

minimumFeedbackCoverage.description: The least `feedbackCoverage` the band is judged on, currently 0.95: below it the band is `insufficient_data`, as bounce and complaint reports are still arriving.

DeliverabilityHealth.description: Advisory bounce and complaint health on the workspace's lines (`limits`): judged once `sampleSize` and `feedbackCoverage` reach their minimums. Bounces and complaints are recorded ones, so a simulated test bounce never counts.

DeliverabilityLimits.description: Where the bands start, the workspace's own lines: `watch` where its admins are warned, `critical` where its marketing email pauses. The pause is judged on all of the workspace's marketing email over the last 24 hours (or week, for a small sender), not on one report.

allChanges.after:
The contact column to test. Each takes these operators, and is refused with others: `email`: equals, notEquals, contains, startsWith, exists, notExists, in; `firstName`: equals, notEquals, contains, startsWith, exists, notExists, in; `lastName`: equals, notEquals, contains, startsWith, exists, notExists, in; `phone`: equals, notEquals, contains, startsWith, exists, notExists, in; `timezone`: equals, notEquals, contains, startsWith, exists, notExists, in; `externalId`: equals, notEquals, contains, startsWith, exists, notExists, in; `consent.email`: equals; `consent.push`: equals; `country`: equals, notEquals, in, exists, notExists; `locale`: equals, notEquals, startsWith, in, exists, notExists; `rfmGroup`: equals, notEquals, in, exists, notExists; `rfmRecency`: equals, notEquals, in, exists, notExists, gt, gte, lt, lte; `rfmFrequency`: equals, notEquals, in, exists, notExists, gt, gte, lt, lte; `rfmMonetary`: equals, notEquals, in, exists, notExists, gt, gte, lt, lte; `purchaseCount`: equals, gt, gte, lt, lte; `totalSpent`: equals, gt, gte, lt, lte; `lastPurchasedAt`: before, after, withinLastDays, moreThanDaysAgo, exists, notExists; `createdAt`: before, after, withinLastDays, moreThanDaysAgo. `phone` holds +country numbers: write `equals`, `notEquals` and `in` values with their country code. Consent takes `true` or `false`.

Purchases: `purchaseCount`, `totalSpent` (in the main currency) and `lastPurchasedAt` are a customer's totals of the workspace's purchase event (`purchaseEvent` in workspace settings: an order, a paid invoice, a booking), recomputed daily; the contact's stored `totalSpent` is null when the workspace's purchases carry no amount. In comparisons on `purchaseCount` and `totalSpent` a missing count or spend is 0, so someone who never purchased has 0 purchases and 0 spent.

RFM: `rfmGroup` and its scores `rfmRecency`, `rfmFrequency` and `rfmMonetary` (monetary value: how much they spend) come from the same daily pass. A score is a whole number from 1 to 5 (an array of them for `in`), 5 being the most recent, most frequent or highest spending; any other value is refused with 400. Someone who never purchased has no `rfmGroup` or scores: on those four fields they match only `notExists` and `notEquals`. So `rfmRecency` `notEquals` 5 includes everyone who never purchased; add an `exists` rule on the same field to leave them out (bought, but not recently).
